Day 83 of 100 · CI/CD & Observability

CI/CD Foundations

#100DaysOfCloudAndSecurityCI/CD & ObservabilityPublished journey entry

CI/CD turns source changes into a repeatable delivery path where validation, build, test and deployment decisions are explicit instead of depending on manual release memory.

Architecture / mental model

commit / pull request → CI checks → build artifact → deployment gate → environment → verification

How it works

Continuous Integration means changes are integrated frequently and checked automatically so failures are detected close to the change that caused them. The checks may include tests, formatting, static analysis, security scanning and build validation depending on the project.

Continuous Delivery keeps the software in a deployable state and makes the path to an environment repeatable. Continuous Deployment goes further by automatically promoting changes that satisfy the defined gates. Those terms are related but not interchangeable.

The pipeline should build a traceable artifact once and promote that artifact rather than rebuilding different code at every stage. Logs, status and artifact identity are part of the evidence trail, not decorative CI badges.

Hands-on reference

git status
git log --oneline -5
# Typical pipeline stages:
# validate → test → build → scan → package → deploy → verify

Verification

Start with a deliberately failing test or validation rule and prove the pipeline stops before packaging/deployment. Then fix the change and verify the exact artifact that passed checks is the one promoted.

Field note / gotcha

A green pipeline only proves the checks you encoded. Missing tests, permissive gates or rebuilding artifacts between stages can automate the wrong outcome very efficiently.

Security considerations

Keep deployment credentials out of repository files, scope CI identities to the minimum environment/actions required, protect branches/environments and treat third-party workflow actions as supply-chain dependencies.

What I learned

A useful pipeline makes failure visible, artifact identity traceable and release behavior repeatable.
